# Save compatibility fixtures

`schema6-expedition.json` is synthetic gameplay state, not user data. It was
produced from the published local v0.12 commit `6a780c4`, using that revision's
actual World, Generator and Expedition implementation in an isolated directory.
It is deliberately not a current map with its version number edited downward.

Reproduction:

1. Export `git archive 6a780c4` into a disposable directory.
2. Run a Godot `SceneTree` script with that directory as `--path`.
3. Construct `World.new(0)`; obtain `Generator.validate(world.floors).route`.
4. Replay each U/D/L/R using `world.step(direction)`, reaching the first ending.
5. Call `world.action("expedition")` once, assert `save_data().version == 6`,
   and write `JSON.stringify(world.save_data())` to the fixture path.

The fixture is at the start of the old eight-floor expedition. It contains no
Mira (`t`) or gaoler (`W`). Schema 7 must preserve its existing maps, classify it
as expedition revision 1, and not mint new rescue progress, gear or camp stock.

## Schema 7 earned rewards

`schema7-expedition.json`, `schema7-repeater.json` and
`schema7-supplies.json` originate from published local commit `4382454`, exported
into an isolated directory. These are synthetic gameplay fixtures, not user saves.
The expedition fixture follows the same first-chapter witness procedure above.
The two reward fixtures replay that revision's `test_rescue.gd` real route:
walk from spawn to J, accept, beat the first chapter, continue, follow the second
chapter witness until just before Z, return to seventh-floor W and rescue t.
From that saved branch, walk back to J and choose `rescue_repeater`, or walk to
sixth-floor U and choose `rescue_supplies`. Capture immediately after each choice.
The supplies capture uses actual stair/path walking to U, not the targeted
resource/position fixtures elsewhere in the test; its three stocks are earned.
The old World writes these files directly with `JSON.stringify(save_data())`.
Schema 8 must add only a fresh oath: maps, earned gear, rescue outcome, money,
loan state and both three-use camp inventories must remain intact.

## Schema 8 oath and reward combinations

`schema8-repeater.json` and `schema8-supplies.json` were written by the actual
World from published local commit `a3b9bdd`, exported into an isolated directory.
Starting from the genuine schema 7 reward fixtures above, its own migration is
applied, then the character walks via real stairs to fourth-floor N. The repeater
branch binds the oath; the supplies branch binds and permanently releases it.
Capture `JSON.stringify(world.save_data())` immediately afterward, asserting
version 8. Neither version numbers nor gameplay fields are manually changed.
These synthetic, non-user fixtures preserve active/spent oath and earned
repeater/three-stock rewards. Their visited floors must not create fast-travel
anchors when migrating to schema 9, nor count as reading/solving the new audit.

## Schema 9 solved audit and registered landmarks

`schema9-medicine.json` and `schema9-retrain.json` originate from published commit
`79d2c803a40004002d28cfd1fb3bb6895bf6a027`, exported into an isolated directory.
Its actual World loads the genuine schema 8 supplies fixture, walks down/up at N,
then via real stairs onto U and Y, registering three landmarks. It performs real
safe fast travel N and back Y, reads the audit and independently enumerates the
three statements to choose the unique answer. From that exact solved snapshot:
medicine chooses `audit_medicine`; retrain learns the three already-earned tiers
(`keen_edge`, `trained_focus`, `battle_medic`) then chooses `audit_retrain`.
No field, map, position, resource or version-number edits are used.
Both preserve spent oath, NPC supplies outcome and stock 3/3. The medicine branch
has 594 moves / 515 HP; the retrain branch 597 moves / 375 HP and cleared talents.
These are synthetic gameplay state, not user saves.

## Schema 10 winch branches awaiting Mira's reward

`schema10-rescue.json` and `schema10-armory.json` were generated by the real World
from published local commit `2efddf937197e9455ad8fafeac39601ec03a5a12`, isolated
using `git archive`. `generate_schema10.gd` is the exact generation script; run it
with that old checkout as Godot's `--path` and create `/tmp/tower-v17-legacy` first.
It starts a fresh seed-0 run, follows the real first-chapter and expedition proof
routes (stopping before Z), and walks back to the winch. The legitimate snapshot
there branches into north rescue without killing W, or armory pickup followed by
normal combat against W. Both then walk via stairs to J but do not claim Mira's
reward. All movement, equipment swaps, choices and combat use actual World APIs;
no field injection, version edits or resource changes are performed.

Rescue: 598 moves / 565 HP, W alive, no maul. Armory: 601 moves / 375 HP, maul
owned, W dead. Both are rescue_state 2 at J, eligible to choose repeater, with no
attunement fields. Synthetic test gameplay only, no user data.

## Schema 11 old and new layout expeditions

`schema11-layout1.json` and `schema11-layout2.json` are produced with the actual
published World from `34af95002022d388314ecf3d2392e220d42cb15a` in an isolated
`git archive` export. `generate_schema11.gd` is the exact generator; run it with
that old export as Godot `--path`, after creating `/tmp/tower-v18-legacy`.

The layout-2 fixture starts a genuine fresh seed-0 game, replays the validated
mainline through World.step, then explicitly continues into the expedition.
It has 242 moves / 277 HP and is on floor six at (9,9).
The layout-1 fixture uses that old World's real migration of the genuine
schema10-armory fixture, then performs the available rescue_repeater action at J.
It has 602 moves / 375 HP, on floor one at (1,2), with both maul and repeater.
Both have an ongoing eight-floor expedition. All state is produced by old World
APIs, not by editing positions, resources or version numbers. No attunement or
persistent profile fields are added. Synthetic gameplay only, not user data.

## Cross-runtime legacy profile protocol vectors

`legacy-profile-vectors.json` contains 37 cases generated by running
`godot --headless --path . --script tools/generate_legacy_vectors.gd` against
`scripts/legacy_profile.gd`. These are synthetic protocol cases, not old game saves
or user progress. They compare GDScript and JavaScript validation/settlement semantics,
including duplicate/conflict, JSON numeric normalization and malformed profiles.
Human-readable error wording is not part of the protocol. The browser storage harness
uses these fixtures without requiring WebGL; passing them does not prove game integration.
